title: Logarithmic Functions
summary: A logarithm inverts an exponential: $\log_b x=y$ means $b^y=x$. The log laws convert products, quotients, and powers into sums, differences, and multiples, and taking a log solves exponential equations for the unknown exponent.

product law.plain: Log of a product is a sum.

quotient law.plain: Log of a quotient is a difference.

power law.plain: Log of a power pulls the exponent out.

change of base.plain: Rewrite a log in another base.

concept_sections.heading: Logarithms as inverses
concept_sections.explanation: $\log_b x$ answers 'what power of $b$ gives $x$?'. It undoes the exponential, so $b^{\log_b x}=x$.

concept_sections.heading: Common and natural logs
concept_sections.explanation: $\log$ means base 10; $\ln$ means base $e$. Calculators provide both, and change-of-base handles any other base.

concept_sections.heading: The log laws
concept_sections.explanation: Products become sums, quotients differences, and powers coefficients: $\log(MN)=\log M+\log N$, etc. Use them to expand or condense.

concept_sections.heading: Solving exponential equations
concept_sections.explanation: Take a logarithm of both sides to bring a variable exponent down, then solve the resulting linear equation.
math_steps: Use the power law and solve.

concept_sections.heading: Solving logarithmic equations
concept_sections.explanation: Condense to a single log, rewrite in exponential form, and solve — then check for extraneous solutions (logs need positive arguments).

real_world_examples.title: The Richter scale
real_world_examples.how_the_math_applies: Each unit is a tenfold energy increase — a base-10 logarithm.

real_world_examples.title: Sound in decibels
real_world_examples.how_the_math_applies: Decibels are $10\log$ of an intensity ratio.

real_world_examples.title: Solving for time in growth
real_world_examples.scenario: How long until an investment doubles?
real_world_examples.how_the_math_applies: Taking a log of $b^t=2$ solves for the time $t$.
